metadata.title: Card Hustle — Dialogue Library V9 (cleaned, cast, with humour layer)
metadata.description: Single self-contained narrative dataset: V2-V6 scenes, ten V1 entry scenes and the entire V1 deep node graph embedded here. Claude audits runtime integration.

editorial_rules.pop_culture_frequency: Rare special variation, not a default or quota; do not trigger more than one conspicuous reference in an encounter.
editorial_rules.ambient_first: Ordinary discussions should heavily outnumber trading talk and pop-culture jokes.
editorial_rules.no_card_topic_leak: Baker, police and other non-collector occupations are not allowed to suddenly discuss card valuation. Explicit personal hobby or relevant job experience required.
editorial_rules.rejoin_guard: Never teleport from a serious topic into jokes or from bakery to card shop. Hubs are optional candidates, not mandatory connections.
editorial_rules.memory: Reuse only when NPC remembers the encounter. Track who learned what, joke reception, prior promises, and whether buyer purchased; do not overwrite economy state.
editorial_rules.player_agency: Walk away at any time; do not fabricate purchases, inventory, condition, prices or negotiated outcomes.
editorial_rules.authenticity: No verbatim franchise catchphrases or unauthorized copyrighted character cameos; review references prior to release.
editorial_rules.finite_content: Not infinite; avoid repeated lines and offer natural endings; expanding authoring is required for depth.

Anytime. That’s customer service.
souhait: Thanks! Same to you.
Thanks. I’ll take it, with a receipt.
empathie: Long shift, short break. The usual.
Busy, but busy is good for business.
compagnie: After closing, maybe. Before closing, I belong to the customers.
depart: Take care. And if you see Curtis, tell him the back door is open.
Bye! Mind the wet floor sign. It means it.
See you next time. There’s always a next time.
blague_ratee: I’ll file that next to the expired coupons.
Cute. Not funny. Cute.
blague_insiste: I’ve worked retail. I can out-wait any joke.
ou_quand: Two doors down from the café. Look for the sign that’s been crooked since spring.

plus: I could tell you, but there’s a form for that.
Officially, no comment. Unofficially, ask me at lunch.
merci: You’re welcome. That one didn’t even need paperwork.
Glad to help. It’s literally my job.
souhait: Thank you. It’s a long list today.
Thanks. Here’s hoping the afternoon is boring.
empathie: Busy. Meetings about meetings.
Fine. Everyone has an urgent question and it’s always the same one.
compagnie: My break is at three. If the phone lets me.
depart: Have a good one. Office hours end at five, patience at four.
Take care. Drive slow by the school.
See you around. Probably at a council meeting.
blague_ratee: I’ll note that in the minutes. Under ‘other business’.
That joke needs a permit.
ou_quand: Check the notice board at City Hall. It’s updated. Mostly.
Today at four, if the council agrees. They rarely agree.

plus: Can’t share details. I can share that it was ridiculous.
Let’s just say it’s in a report now.
merci: Anytime. Stay safe.
That’s what we’re here for.
souhait: Thanks. Quiet days are the best days.
Appreciated. Fingers crossed for no sirens.
empathie: Long shift. Nothing exploded, so it was a good one.
Tired, but everyone went home fine.
compagnie: Sure, if the radio stays quiet.
depart: Stay safe out there.
Take care. And look both ways, I mean it.
See you. Hopefully not professionally.
blague_ratee: I’ve heard worse on night shift.
Filed under harmless.
blague_insiste: I’m trained to stay calm. Even now.
ou_quand: Near the station, you’ll see the trucks.
It’s happening at noon. Unless something catches fire.

plus: Oh, that’s a long story. Sit down, I’ll make it longer.
Back in my day, we had the same story, just slower.
merci: You’re a good kid. Your grandmother raised you right. Whoever she is.
Anytime, dear. I have nothing but time.
souhait: Thank you, dear. At my age, every day is a bonus round.
You too. Don’t work too hard.
empathie: My knees complain, my heart’s fine.
Better now. Talking is good for the old engine.
compagnie: Sit, sit. The bench has room and I have stories.
depart: Off you go. Say hello to your parents.
Take care, sweetheart. Wear a jacket.
Go on, young people are always running somewhere.
blague_ratee: Ha! I didn’t get it, but I liked your face while telling it.
My late brother told that one better. In 1974.
blague_insiste: Keep going, I’ll laugh eventually. I’m patient.
ou_quand: By the fountain, where the old hardware store used to be.
This afternoon. Or tomorrow. I wrote it on a napkin.

plus: Okay so, okay so, it’s a secret but I’ll tell you everything.
I can’t tell you. I can tell you a little. Okay, everything.
merci: You’re welcome! Do you want to know about beetles now?
Yay! I helped!
souhait: You too! Have the best day ever. Or second best.
Thanks! Mine is already great because recess.
empathie: I’m fine! I fell but I didn’t cry. Much.
Good! I had pancakes!
compagnie: Yes! You can be on my team!
depart: Bye! Bye! Okay bye!
See you! Don’t tell anyone my secret!
Bye! I’m going to run there, not walk.
blague_ratee: That was so bad it was funny.
I don’t get it. Tell it again!
ou_quand: Over there! No, there! By the big fountain!

plus: Honestly? It’s a whole saga.
You don’t want the lore. Trust me, you want the lore.
merci: No problem.
Yeah, sure. Anytime.
souhait: Thanks. Same.
You too, I guess.
empathie: I’m good. Tired. School-tired.
Fine. My parents asked me the same thing. Twice.
compagnie: Sure, just don’t make it weird.
depart: Later.
See ya.
Cool. Bye.
blague_ratee: That was so dad-coded.
Respectfully, no.
blague_insiste: Okay, it was kind of funny. Don’t tell anyone.
ou_quand: By the courts. Or the café. Somewhere with Wi-Fi.

plus: Let me put it this way: condition is everything, and that story was mint.
There’s more, but I don’t give away information for free. Kidding. Mostly.
merci: Anytime. Knowledge is the only thing I share without a price tag.
Sure. Just don’t quote me on prices.
souhait: Thanks. May your pulls be shiny.
You too. And sleeve your cards.
empathie: Fine. The market’s moody, so I’m moody.
It’s been a long day of people saying ‘it’s rare’.
compagnie: Sure, if you don’t mind me sorting while we talk.
depart: See you at the next market.
Later. Check your corners.
Take care. Don’t buy anything shiny on impulse.
blague_ratee: I’d grade that joke a four. Light play, visible wear.
Common. Very common.
blague_insiste: You’re trying to inflate that joke’s value. I see you.
ou_quand: At the card shop, Linh will know.
Saturday morning, the big market. Be early, the resellers are.

plus: Everything on this table has a story. Some of them are even true.
Oh, you want the story? That’s free. The lamp is five dollars.
merci: Anytime, dear. Take a look around while you’re here.
My pleasure. Tell your friends, we take cash.
souhait: Thanks! Hope you find a treasure.
You too. And if you see a lost lid, it’s mine.
empathie: Sorting a whole life into boxes. It’s a lot.
Long morning. Everybody wants a discount and a story.
compagnie: Stay a minute. You’re good for business, you look curious.
depart: Come back before noon, everything gets cheaper.
Bye! Tell your parents we’re here till three.
See you. Don’t forget, everything must go.
blague_ratee: I’ll sell that joke for a quarter. No refunds.
Even the fondue set laughed harder.
blague_insiste: Keep it up and I’ll make you buy the lamp.
ou_quand: Wednesday around the fountain, Saturday on the big square.

plus: Long story short: someone pushed the wrong button. Long story long: same, with diagrams.
The technical answer is boring. The real answer is ‘it was Doug’.
merci: Sure. If it breaks again, it wasn’t me.
No problem. Turn it off and on again, works on most things.
souhait: Thanks. Here’s to nothing breaking.
Appreciated. It’s been a two-coffee problem kind of day.
empathie: Fixed one thing, found three more. Normal day.
Fine. The machine won this round, I win tomorrow.
compagnie: Sure, hand me that wrench while you’re here.
depart: See you. Don’t touch anything blinking.
Later. Label your stuff.
Take care. And close the gate, please.
blague_ratee: That joke needs maintenance.
Error 404: punchline not found.
blague_insiste: I’ve debugged worse. Not much worse.
ou_quand: Up by the wind turbines. Follow the humming.
Behind the hardware store, the gate with the sign nobody reads.

plus: I just got here and already have a notebook full of stories.
Everyone here talks like the town is a sitcom. I’m starting to believe it.
merci: Thanks! People here are so friendly. Suspiciously friendly.
Thank you, that’s really helpful.
souhait: Thanks! You too.
Thank you! I’ll try to see the water tower before I go.
empathie: Good! Just a little lost. Charmingly lost.
Great, honestly. Small towns are restful.
compagnie: I’d love that. You can tell me which stories are true.
depart: Bye! Maybe I’ll see you at the market.
Take care! I’m off to sketch the water tower again.
See you around. Literally, the town is small.
blague_ratee: Is that a local joke? I feel like I’m missing context.
I’ll laugh once I figure out where the punchline went.
blague_insiste: Okay, you’re officially the town comedian.
ou_quand: Somewhere near the fountain, I think. Everything here is near the fountain.

humour.note: Humour pop culture de Card Hustle. Règles d'écriture : allusions reconnaissables, jamais de réplique culte recopiée mot pour mot, pas de nom de personnage ou de marque dans le texte dit (le champ 'reference' sert seulement à l'audit). Chaque réplique a un public (âge), des goûts (ce que le personnage connaît) et une intensité (1 = clin d'œil discret, 2 = blague franche, 3 = gros gag) ; le directeur d'humour décide si et quand elle sort.

repliques.texte: Oh, there’s a whole side quest. It ends with me fetching ten mushrooms for nobody.
That story has three endings. Depends on what dialogue option you pick.
The lore runs deep. Like, collect-every-scattered-diary-page deep.
Previously, on This Town…
It’s a long story. Like, extended-edition-with-appendices long.
I’d tell you, but then the plot twist wouldn’t hit as hard.
That’s canon. Everything after that is fan theory.
Okay, but first you need the context. And the context needs context.
The full story unlocks at friendship level three.
repliques.reference: jauges d'amitié des simulations de vie

repliques.texte: My grandson says it ‘has lore’. I think that means it’s complicated.
In this house we call that a rare drop. As in, it rarely happens and then drops on you.
There’s more, but you have to watch until after the credits.
Achievement unlocked: actually listening.
Glad to help. Consider it a free tutorial.
Tip of the day: never trust a crate in a game, or a free sample at the market.
You’re welcome. Your quest log has been updated.
Happy to help. I’m basically the friendly shopkeeper in the first village.
Anytime. Wisdom: plus one.
No problem. My granddaughter would say I ‘carried’. I carried groceries mostly.
Thanks. Here’s hoping today doesn’t have a final boss.
You too. May your loading screens be short.
Thanks. I’ll save my progress just in case.
Thanks. Everything is fine. That’s what the dog in the burning room said too.
repliques.reference: chien dans la pièce en feu

repliques.texte: You too. Main character energy, okay?
Honestly? My stamina bar is flashing red.
Let’s just say my needs bars are all orange.
repliques.reference: jauges de besoins des simulations de vie

repliques.texte: It’s fine. Everything is fine. Small fire, very calm dog.
repliques.reference: chien dans la pièce en feu

repliques.texte: Today felt like a level where you can’t pause.
I died a few times, but I respawned at the coffee machine.
Tired. Like a hero after the training montage, minus the muscles.
Rough day. The kids would say it was ‘an emotional damage situation’. I just say Tuesday.
I’m okay. No thoughts, head empty, just vibes.
Sure. Party member joined.
Another time. Let’s say I’ll be at the same spot, same hour, like a well-scripted villager.
Co-op mode? Sure. You hold the bags.
See you. Don’t forget to save.
Bye! I’ll be right here, standing in the exact same spot. As one does.
Go on. Your quest marker is blinking.
Later. Don’t fast-travel into a wall.
Take care. Heading out alone? Here, take a snack. Every hero starts with one item.
repliques.reference: allusion au vieil homme de la grotte

repliques.texte: See you. I’ll pretend this conversation never happened, spy-movie style.
Bye. Touch some grass on the way, it’s free.
Off you go. My grandson says ‘GG’. I believe it means good luck.
That joke needed a patch before release.
Critical miss.
Roll for charisma. Oh. Oh no.
Skill issue. Comedy skill, specifically.
I can hear the sitcom laugh track refusing to play.
That one’s getting a one-star review.
Common rarity. Heavily played.
You’re grinding that joke like it’s going to level up.
Interesting strategy. The crowd remains unconvinced.
This is your villain origin story, isn’t it?
Follow the fountain. Everything here is one fast-travel point.
By the square. If you reach the edge of the map, you went too far.

receptions.note: Réaction d'un personnage quand le joueur choisit un ton joueur ou absurde, selon son style d'humour. 'rit' si le personnage aime ce genre de blague, 'poli' sinon, 'plat' quand ce n'est vraiment pas le moment (émotion négative, négociation tendue).

rit: Okay, that was decent. Don’t let it go to your head.
Ha. Fine. One point to you.
poli: I’m laughing on the inside. Deep inside.
Somebody write that down. Then lose it.
I see what you did there. I’m choosing not to react.
plat: Let’s keep it serious for a minute.

poli: Heh, you’re in a mood today.

rit: Hahaha! Wait, why is it funny? Hahaha!
poli: I don’t get it but okay!

rit: Oh, I’m telling that one at dinner.
That’s a good one, I’ll steal it.
poli: You’re in a good mood today.

rit: Ha! Nice reference. I’m counting it.
poli: I get the reference. I just don’t respect it.
Mid, but I see the effort.
Two out of five stars. Generous.

rit: Ha! That’s one of those internet jokes, isn’t it? I love those.
Oh, you young people and your bits!
Ha! You remind me of my brother. He was trouble too.
Oh, that’s a good one. I won’t remember it, but it’s good.
poli: I’ll laugh once my grandson explains it.
Is that a meme? It feels like a meme.

etapes.texte: Six ducks refused to leave the crosswalk this morning. Traffic stopped. The ducks did not care.
The ducks are back. One of them stared at me like I owed it money.
The ducks now cross in formation. I think they have a leader. I think it has a plan.
Final report on the ducks: they won. We put up a sign. They ignore the sign.

running_gags.titre: La Bourse de Tyler et Noah

etapes.texte: Noah and I opened a trading desk. It’s a bench, but it’s a professional bench.
Market update: shiny dragons are up two juice boxes. Bugs are down. Bugs are always down.
We had a crash. Mason traded a holo for a dinosaur sticker. Noah needs a minute.
We recovered! The market loves dinosaurs now. Mason is a genius. Or lucky. Noah says lucky.
Try the sauce. Don’t comment on the sauce. Just try the sauce.
Mike says his barbecue sauce is better. Mike is wrong, and Mike knows it.
The recipe is locked in a safe. The safe is locked in my head. My head is locked to Mike.
Fine. One secret ingredient. It’s patience. And a lot of paprika. Mostly paprika.
Has anyone seen my good wrench? Not the other good wrench. The good one.
Jamie labeled every tool in the shed. Every single one. Even the label maker has a label.
Found the wrench. It was in my hand. For two days. Don’t tell Carol.
Doug lent the wrench again. We’re starting a tracking system. It has a spreadsheet and a prayer.
I averaged every price this month. The average is lying, but consistently.
Ben says I forgot condition again. My spreadsheet has feelings now. Column G is called Regret.
I added a column for language. Then one for ‘vibes’. Ben is concerned.
The spreadsheet crashed. I stared at it like the end of a sad movie. It was beautiful.
That water tower has incredible lighting at six. I’ve taken two hundred photos.
Antonio says he helped build it. He also says he built half the town. I’m starting to believe him.
I think the water tower is the town’s final boss. Nobody has seen the top.
Antonio took me up. The top has a chair, a thermos and a 1983 newspaper. Legend confirmed.
The bus leaves at 8:10. Not 8:11. The bus is not a negotiation.
Someone asked me to wait one minute. I said: this is a bus, not a loading screen.
Gloria says I’m strict. Gloria once left the mayor at a bus stop. In the rain. On his birthday.
Stalls open at seven. Not seven-ish. Seven. I printed it in bold.
I added rule fourteen: no haggling with a dramatic speech about destiny. You know who you are.
Patricia contradicted me in front of everyone. She was right. That’s not the point. The point is the rules.
